name: Mumbai Nagar Seva — BMC Civic Complaint Resolution 2018–2024 (Kaggle competition data)
publisher: As listed on Kaggle (competition host not verified). NOT verified as an official BMC / Government of Maharashtra open-data source or API.
role_summary: Primary Indian structured civic source: analytics, recurrence/hotspots, taxonomy coverage, department/category mapping, SLA/triage priors, realistic demos — pending provenance and licence verification.
version_note: Per a web-search summary of the Kaggle data page (secondary): ~1.2M complaints, Jan 2018–Dec 2024, all 24 BMC wards; files bmc_train.csv (960,000 rows, 35 features + target `citizen_satisfied`), bmc_test.csv (240,000 rows, 34 features, target WITHHELD) and bmc_data_dictionary.csv. Feature groups reported: geography, complaint type, filing channel, severity, complainant profile, resolution process, contractor details, infrastructure context. Competition task: predict citizen satisfaction with the resolution. Only the train file can be used for local supervised evaluation; the exact column names are NOT known to us.

data_access.method: Kaggle competition data: accept the competition rules on Kaggle, then attach it as a notebook input or use the Kaggle CLI with YOUR credentials. This repository never downloads it.
data_access.data_dictionary: bmc_data_dictionary.csv ships with the data: read it, then assign every column to a role explicitly (see mappings/bmc_mumbai_columns.v1.json and `cli profile bmc_mumbai`).

license.name: Kaggle competition rules / data-use terms for this competition — NOT READ

evidence.source: web search summary of the Kaggle data page
evidence.note: Describes the files and task; states no licence in the summary.

license.attribution: Cite the Kaggle competition page and its host exactly as the Rules require (not read).
notes: Read the competition Rules ('Data Access and Use') before ANY use outside the competition; if the rules restrict use to the competition, this source may not be usable for CivicConnect at all.

origin_notes: Fixed 35-feature schema, 1.2M rows, 24 wards, a binary target and a train/test split indicate a competition-curated dataset. Nothing verified states whether the rows are real BMC complaint records, a simulation, or a modelled/derived dataset.

Do not describe this as official BMC data, a BMC API, or a government open-data release until its provenance is independently verified (read the competition description and data dictionary; check the host).
If it turns out to be synthetic/simulated, re-label it kind=synthetic: it then supports plumbing/analytics demos only and NO real-world claim.
subset_used: Train file only. For development a bounded deterministic sample (prepare --max-rows N --sample-seed S); full 960k rows only if resources and rules permit. Time-based holdout (most recent months).
restrictions: Competition rules not read; assume NO redistribution and possibly competition-only use until verified.
Complainant-profile columns are sensitive attributes: they must never be features or targets for any task (system design §13). The adapter never stores them.
Contractor/officer/address/contact columns can identify people or firms: the adapter never reads them (PII roles).
Post-resolution fields (status, closing time, resolution remarks, reassignment, escalation, satisfaction/rating) must never be inputs for intake or triage — see the per-task column policy.
Do not commit raw or prepared rows.

supports.how: Validate deterministic recurrence/hotspot/baseline analytics on a large Indian ward-level spatio-temporal complaint set; seed realistic demo data.
caveats: Provenance (real vs simulated) unverified: no real-world claim until verified.

supports.how: Routing/department-mapping agreement against our taxonomy, and resolution-time / triage-time priors (descriptive) to sanity-check SLA hours and priority score ranges.
caveats: Severity/priority labels may be derived from category or process: a determinism check is mandatory before any use as a target.
Resolution times are right-censored for unresolved complaints.

supports.how: Realistically distributed rows to seed a copilot demo database (labelled as unverified-origin data).
caveats: Demo realism only; not a model evaluation.

does_not_support.why: No verified citizen-written free text is known to exist in the columns; if a description column exists it must be inspected and explicitly confirmed as citizen text, and must not echo the label.

does_not_support.capability: AI-1 image intake / AI-4 resolution evidence
does_not_support.why: Tabular data: no images, no before/after evidence. 'Resolution process' fields are workflow metadata, not evidence.
Severity is a competition feature of unknown provenance, not an independently validated label.
Post-resolution outcome; not part of CivicConnect V1 (no reputation/satisfaction scoring); its test labels are withheld.

known_limitations: Competition curation may differ from raw operational data (sampling, cleaning, simulation).
Timestamp semantics (filing vs registration vs closure) must be read from the data dictionary.
privacy_notes: Complainant profile, contractor and any address/contact/officer columns are excluded by policy (never stored).
expected_schema_notes: User-reported complaint categories (not verified against the file): Pothole/Road Damage; Water Supply Disruption; Solid Waste/Garbage; Drainage Overflow/Flooding; Street Light Failure; Illegal Construction; Encroachment; Tree Fallen/Dangerous Tree; Public Toilet Condition; Water Leakage/Pipe Burst; Noise/Air Pollution; Stray Animal Menace; Health/Epidemic.
Exact column names unknown. The adapter resolves roles by alias and by an explicit operator-supplied --role-map; every other column is 'unclassified' and default-denied.
